title: Egress policy sync heuristics — oncall journal & runbook draft
content:
SUMMARY:

This is an on-call journal / early runbook draft capturing our response to intermittent customer control-plane reachability and application-level egress failures traced to delayed policy propagation (egress rules) in Private/VPC customers running on our on-prem appliance mesh. Issue surfaced 2026-11-21 07:42 UTC when multiple alerts from the control-plane health probes and customer support tickets indicated application timeouts for outbound HTTPS traffic.

Scope & Impact:
- Affected customers: 3 active Private deployments in APAC region (tenant ids masked).
- Symptoms: outbound connections (443) from tenant workloads intermittently failing with TCP RST or long connect times (2–6s), control-plane API heartbeat drops from worker nodes to control-plane (0.5–2% error bursts).
- Customer-visible impact: degraded app response times, some background jobs timed out and retried. No data loss detected.

Initial hypothesis (first 90m):
- Policy replication delay between control-plane and on-prem agents caused ephemeral egress blocks; possible interaction with DPI appliance that rate-limits new conntrack entries.
- Alternate: control-plane-side throttling triggered by a recent policy sweep (scheduled rollout) that accidentally used a large batch window.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-11-21 07:42 — Pager: SRE oncall (Priya) receives multi-tenant alerts (latency spikes + connect failures).
- 07:45 — Triage started in #oncall-private-vpc channel. Captured first customer trace and tcpdump.
- 07:52 — Verified control-plane leader stable; however, some control-plane agents reported 502s from appliance management endpoint.
- 08:05 — Observed spike in control-plane policy-change-events (600 events in 30s) correlating with increase in conntrack table growth on appliances.
- 08:18 — Applied temporary mitigation: increased conntrack limits on affected appliances; immediate drop in RST rates for one tenant.
- 08:35 — Confirmed a cancelled bulk policy rollout (CLI job) coincided with event spike; rollout had been started by SE team as a validation test and not properly scoped.
- 09:10 — Coordinated with SE + infra to throttle future rollout batch sizes; started drafting automated rollout-safety checks.

Diagnostics & evidence collected:
- Sample tcpdump (redacted): SYN->SYN/ACK delays ~300ms; some SYNs followed by RST.
- Appliance conntrack stats: entries jumped from ~18k to 95k (limit 100k) during burst; lru prune activity increased.
- Control-plane logs: policy-publisher repeatedly reattempting push with partial ACKs; code path showed full policy blob being sent on every incremental change due to missing delta logic (service: policy-publisher v0.9.12).
- Recent deploys: policy-publisher rolled 2026-11-20 22:04 UTC (PR #1280) adding a new "force-sync" flag which defaulted to true in internal test harness.

Root cause (working hypothesis):
A combination of an inadvertent SE-triggered validation job that made many small policy edits and a policy-publisher behavior that aggressively pushed full policy blobs to appliances. This caused a transient explosion in conntrack usage and appliance-side DPI/conntrack pruning, resulting in aborted outbound connections and intermittent control-plane heartbeat failures.

Immediate mitigations performed (what worked):
1) Temporarily increased conntrack and netfilter thresholds on affected appliances (commands below).
2) Reverted the internal validation job and paused SE ad-hoc rollouts while we triage.
3) Rolled back policy-publisher to v0.9.11 on the control-plane leader to restore delta-push behavior.
4) Added temporary acceptance rule in the control-plane to rate-limit policy push events per tenant (soft throttling).

Commands used (examples — redact tenant ids in runbook):
- ssh admin@appliance-XX "sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000"
- ssh admin@appliance-XX "sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=86400"
- kubectl -n control-plane rollout undo deployment/policy-publisher --to-revision=2026-11-20-3
- kubectl -n control-plane logs deploy/policy-publisher -f --since=2h | grep force-sync

Draft runbook steps (to be hardened):
1) Detection: alert thresholds for conntrack growth and policy-push QPS per tenant. Add composite alert: conntrack growth + outbound RST rate > threshold.
2) First response: identify affected appliances via metrics (appliance.conntrack_entries > 80% of limit). Evacuate heavy-churn workloads if possible to another pool.
3) Short-term mitigation: increase conntrack thresholds (if headroom available) and enable L4 bypass for known control-plane health-check sources.
4) Rollback controls: expose a one-click rollback of policy-publisher binary and a rapid toggle for "delta-only" pushes.
5) Throttling: implement API-side rate limiter per-tenant for policy-change events with circuit-breaker to prevent ripple effects.
6) Postmortem: collect tcpdumps, conntrack snapshots, and push history; mark customer incidents with clear timeline and RFO.

Longer-term actions (owners assigned):
- Engineering (Marcus Yu): add delta-generation test and canary gate to policy-publisher; create unit test for force-sync flag default behavior (target: 2 weeks).
- Platform (Lena Hu): add per-tenant policy-change QPS metrics and synthetic test harness that simulates 1k small edits/min (target: 3 weeks).
- SRE (Priya): author the runbook and add automated remediation playbook to the oncall runbook library (target: 1 week).

Notes to self / things to validate later:
- Confirm if DPI appliances have hard conntrack bugs when pruning many TCP entries — vendor ticket needed.
- Correlate with network device telemetry (SNMP) for CPU spikes during event window.
- Check if other teams had scheduled "housekeeping" jobs that touch policies (billing/cleanup cron).

Open questions:
- Should we adopt default "delta-only" push policy globally, or gate behind a config per-tenant? Pros/cons discussion needed with product.
- How to surface policy-change QPS to customers so SEs can avoid ad-hoc high-frequency validation on production tenants?

Communication & customer follow-up
- Drafted customer note for affected tenants summarizing root cause and steps taken; to be reviewed by support lead before send.
- Recommended offering backlog item: a safemode flag for SE validation tenants to route validation to sandbox rather than prod.

Appendix: quick checklist for oncall (condensed):
- Step 0: Confirm alerts and capture metric graphs (conntrack size, outbound RST rate, policy-publisher QPS).
- Step 1: Identify and pause any ad-hoc policy batches.
- Step 2: If conntrack > 80%, run increase command and consider temporarily putting L4 bypass for health probes.
- Step 3: If policy-publisher shows force-sync pushes, roll back to previous stable and throttle pushes.
- Step 4: Collect artifacts and open INFR-3421 with logs and tcpdumps attached.

This doc is intentionally concise — meant to be a quick reference for future oncall rotations and to seed a fuller postmortem. Feedback welcome in the doc comments or ping me directly in #oncall-private-vpc.

-- Priya
